approach: Moment of a force about a point equals the force times the perpendicular distance from that point to the line of the force.

steps.text: Place A at the origin, B at (2,0), C at (2,2), D at (0,2), so O is at (1,1). Each force lies along one side of the square.
About A: the 3 N force (along DA) and the 2 N force (along AB) both act along lines that pass through A itself, so their moment about A is zero.
steps.equation: moment of 3 N about A = 0, moment of 2 N about A = 0

steps.text: About A: the 4 N force (along DC, height 2 m above A) gives moment = force × perpendicular distance.
steps.equation: moment of 4 N about A = 4 × 2 = 8 N·m, clockwise

steps.text: About A: the 5 N force (along CB, 2 m to the side of A) gives its moment the same way.
steps.equation: moment of 5 N about A = 5 × 2 = 10 N·m, clockwise

steps.text: About O: each force's line is now 1 m from O (since O is the centre of the 2 m square), so every moment has magnitude force × 1 m.
steps.equation: perpendicular distance from O to every side = 1 m

steps.text: Work out the turning sense of each force about O from the diagram and multiply by 1 m.
steps.equation: 4 N: 4 N·m clockwise; 3 N: 3 N·m anticlockwise; 5 N: 5 N·m clockwise; 2 N: 2 N·m anticlockwise

final_answer.value: (a) about A: 4 N force = 8 N·m clockwise, 3 N force = 0, 5 N force = 10 N·m clockwise, 2 N force = 0. (b) about O: 4 N force = 4 N·m clockwise, 3 N force = 3 N·m anticlockwise, 5 N force = 5 N·m clockwise, 2 N force = 2 N·m anticlockwise

common_mistakes.text: Taking a nonzero moment for the 3 N and 2 N forces about A, missing that their lines of action pass through A itself.
Using the side length 2 m as the moment arm about O instead of the correct 1 m distance from the centre to each side.
